title: Open a chart and change its timeframe
summary: Open a EUR/USD [[candlestick]] chart and switch between M15, H1, H4 and D1 to see how the same prices look on each [[timeframe]].

steps.text: Check you are on your demo account before you start.
In the Quotes tab, tap EUR/USD and choose the option to open its chart. You can also open the Chart tab and pick the symbol there.
If the chart shows bars or a line, switch it to candlesticks. The chart type is usually in the chart settings or in a menu at the top of the chart. It depends on your app version.
Find the timeframe control. It is usually a label such as H1 at the top of the chart, or a round menu that appears when you tap the chart. It depends on your app version.
steps.mt4: In MT4, tapping the chart often shows a round menu with the timeframes around it.
steps.mt5: In MT5, the timeframe is often shown as a label or button at the top of the chart.

steps.text: Choose M15. Note roughly how many hours of price the screen shows.
Switch to H1, then H4, then D1. Each time, note whether the last part of the chart looks like it is rising, falling or moving sideways.
Pinch to zoom out on D1 to see more candles, then switch back to H1.
Write down one sentence for each timeframe describing what you saw.

afterQuestions.prompt: The last price was the same on every timeframe. Why did the charts look different?

options.text: Each candle covers a different length of time
options.explanation: Right: the same prices are grouped into bigger or smaller candles.
No: it is the same market, grouped differently.

afterQuestions.prompt: H4 looked like it was rising and M15 looked like it was falling. Which is right?

options.text: Both: they cover different windows of time
options.explanation: Right: a short fall can sit inside a longer rise.
No: neither timeframe is the true one.
